sourcing_notes: All three recorded sources were fetched from this container on 2026-09-18 with curl -sL -A "Mokaair-editorial"; no personal data in any header, query string or form. Observed: https://mistral.ai/news/mistral-x-mozilla/ 200 / 243,456 bytes (requested without the trailing slash and redirected to the slashed URL, which is what is recorded); https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/mozilla-mistral-partnership/ 200 / 69,671 bytes; https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/firefox-smart-window/ 200 / 71,906 bytes. All three returned real body. TWO FIRST PARTIES, TWO DIFFERENT ACCOUNTS - this is the defining feature of this record and the reason it is worth writing carefully. Mistral and Mozilla published on the same day and do not say the same thing about which markets get what, or about which model is involved. Both are official. Neither may be picked as the single answer. HOW THE PAGES WERE FOUND, because it is not obvious: mistral.ai/news has no feed and no ISO dates in its markup - the listing prints human dates like 'September 16, 2026' and the article URL had to be recovered from the surrounding HTML (a first guess at /news/mistral-mozilla-firefox returned 404 / 241,752 bytes, i.e. a soft 404 that still serves a full page, so byte count alone would not have revealed the error). Mozilla does have a working feed: https://blog.mozilla.org/en/feed/ returned 200 with 20 items, newest Thu, 17 Sep 2026 19:30:00 +0000. A first guess at https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/firefox-smart-window-mistral/ also returned 404 (51,186 bytes) - both guessed URLs are recorded here so nobody re-derives them, per the BRIEF's rule that a guessed URL is fabrication even when it resolves. LIVE-DOCUMENT WARNING: https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/firefox-smart-window/ is an August post carrying a dated update at the top; its content on 2026-09-18 includes an 'Update on September 16, 2026' block, and more updates can be stacked on it without the URL changing. SOURCE TYPO PRESERVED: Mistral's own post writes 'Mistal's scientific innovations' in the body while the CEO quote at the foot of the same page writes 'Mistral's'. That misspelling is in the published text and any verbatim quote must keep it. No news media, aggregator or search snippet was used.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral published this on 2026-09-16 with a joint byline; the page prints the date and 'By Mistral and Mozilla' under the title.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: September 16, 2026 By Mistral and Mozilla

verified_facts.fact: What was announced, in Mistral's opening sentence: a partnership with Mozilla aimed at people using AI to browse.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Today, we are announcing a partnership with Mozilla to bring privacy, control and choice to people using AI to browse online.

verified_facts.fact: What Firefox Smart Window is, in Mistral's description, and that it is a beta: an AI browsing assistant that helps make sense of complex searches, remember something clicked away from, and source information based on browser tabs.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Smart Window helps you make sense of complex searches, remember something important you clicked away from and source information important to you based on your browser tabs.

verified_facts.fact: MISTRAL'S MARKET SENTENCE, which is one of the two that do not match Mozilla's: France and North America now, with the United Kingdom and Germany 'expected to follow later this year'.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Mistral will help power Smart Window for users in France and North America, with the United Kingdom and Germany expected to follow later this year.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral names no model version anywhere in its post - it says only 'Mistral models', plural and unnumbered.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Firefox Smart Window (beta), Mozilla’s AI browsing assistant, is now powered by Mistral models.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral's framing of why the partnership matters, in a sentence that contains the company's own misspelling of its name ('Mistal') in the published text.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: This partnership represents two open source advocates working together to bring Mistal’s scientific innovations to consumers around the world.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral's multilingual claim, which is the part most relevant to a reader outside Europe and North America: it says it fine-tunes models on regional languages and dialects so people get responses that understand local nuance. No language is named.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: We are building AI systems that are trained and fine-tuned on regional languages, dialects and cultural context, so anyone can get responses that understand their local nuance.

verified_facts.fact: THE TWO DATA TERMS, stated by Mistral and the most checkable thing in the whole announcement: conversations are not saved on Mozilla's servers by default, and partners including Mistral agree to zero data retention.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Privacy protections are built into how Firefox Smart Window works: conversations aren’t saved on Mozilla’s servers by default, and partners like Mistral agree to zero data retention.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral states its own usual market and why this is different for it: it traditionally focuses on serving the enterprise, and reaches consumers here through an ecosystem partner.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: While we traditionally focus on serving the enterprise, by partnering with ecosystem leaders like Firefox, we extend beyond businesses and reach their consumers worldwide.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral's CEO is quoted by name on its own page, and the quote spells the company correctly, unlike the body text above it.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Arthur Mensch, co-founder and CEO of Mistral

verified_facts.fact: Mozilla published the same partnership on the same day; its page prints 'September 16, 2026' under the title and is filed under Firefox.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: September 16, 2026

verified_facts.fact: MOZILLA'S MARKET SENTENCE, which is the other half of the mismatch. Mozilla names the model - Mistral Small 4 - and splits the geography differently: the model is for Smart Window users in the US and Canada, while France gets expanded beta access and French-language support.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: becoming a new AI model for Smart Window users in the US and Canada, while expanding Smart Window beta access and French-language support to Firefox users in France

verified_facts.fact: Mozilla does NOT name the United Kingdom or Germany. Its forward-looking sentence is unnamed and Europe-wide.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: France is the first new market for Smart Window with official French-language support. Mozilla is planning additional European expansion later this year.

verified_facts.fact: The choice condition, which is the point Mozilla is actually making: Mistral is an added option, not a replacement, and users keep other models.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Across all markets where Smart Window beta is available, Firefox users can still choose from a multitude of other AI models.

verified_facts.fact: Why Mozilla says it picked this model: it evaluated Mistral Small 4's performance for Smart Window Beta, with multilingual performance named as an important part of the fit.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Mozilla selected Mistral Small 4 after evaluating its performance for Smart Window Beta, including multilingual performance, an important part of the fit.

verified_facts.fact: Mozilla's own framing of the problem it says the partnership addresses - competition over which models people can reach, not which model is best.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Practically overnight, competition has expanded from “which AI model is best?” to a new high-stakes battle over which models people can access, through which products, and whether people have meaningful choice about AI at all.

verified_facts.fact: Mozilla's CEO is quoted by name and title, arguing that the browser should be a place where different AI providers compete.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: said Anthony Enzor-DeMeo, CEO of Mozilla Corporation

verified_facts.fact: Mozilla states the two-sided arrangement in one line, which is the clearest statement of what each party gets.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Mistral can reach Firefox users without owning the browser, and Mozilla can integrate and recommend Mistral without removing user choice.

verified_facts.fact: The August Smart Window post carries a dated update that gives a third, independent account of what happened on 2026-09-16 - and it says France is Smart Window's FIRST expansion beyond North America.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Update on September 16, 2026: Smart Window is now rolling out in France, marking its first expansion beyond North America.

verified_facts.fact: What Smart Window is, in Mozilla's own definition, including the consent condition on the context it uses: open tabs and relevant browsing history that the user chooses to share.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: It works with the context you choose to share, such as your open tabs and relevant browsing history, so you can get back to what you were doing without retracing your steps.

verified_facts.fact: Mistral is not the only outside model supplier named around Smart Window. Mozilla's August post announces a partnership with Exa for retrieving current web information and showing sources.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: Through our new partnership with Exa, Smart Window can now retrieve current web information and show the sources behind its response without taking you to a separate search results page.

verified_facts.fact: Mozilla's Head of Firefox, Ajit Varma, is quoted in the August post on what Smart Window is exploring.
verified_facts.verbatim_quote: With Smart Window, we’re exploring how to make more of that context useful while keeping you in control.

not_said: TAIWAN IS NOT NAMED BY EITHER COMPANY, and no Asian market is named at all. As checked on all three pages to 2026-09-18, the only places named are France, North America / the US and Canada, the United Kingdom and Germany. The article must write '兩家公司都沒有提到台灣或任何亞洲市場' and must NOT write that Smart Window is unavailable in Taiwan - neither company publishes an exclusion list, and Mozilla says Smart Window beta exists in markets it does not enumerate.

No release date, version or channel for Firefox. Neither company says which Firefox version contains Smart Window, whether it is a separate download, or how a user checks whether they have it. Mozilla's August post links a 'Download Smart Window here' and gives no version.

No language list. Mistral claims fine-tuning on regional languages and dialects but names none. Mozilla names French only. Whether Traditional Chinese is supported at any level is not addressed anywhere.
No price, and no statement about whether any of this is or will remain free.

No detail on the zero-data-retention term: no duration, no scope, no audit, no statement of which requests it covers, and no named agreement. Mistral writes 'partners like Mistral agree to zero data retention' - a description of an arrangement, not a published policy.
No explanation of 'by default' in 'conversations aren't saved on Mozilla's servers by default'. Neither page says what turns that default off, or who can.
No benchmark, score or evaluation result. Mozilla says it evaluated Mistral Small 4's performance; it publishes no number, no comparison and no methodology.
No list of the other models a Firefox user can choose. Mozilla says users can still choose from 'a multitude of other AI models' and names none of them.
No commercial terms - no statement of who pays whom, whether this is a default, a recommendation or a paid placement, or how long it runs.
No user numbers, no adoption figures, no beta participant count.

No mention of any regulator, of the EU's Digital Markets Act, or of any competition proceeding, despite both posts being framed around competition and choice. Neither company names a law or an authority.

unverified_or_excluded.seen_where: Mistral: 'France and North America, with the United Kingdom and Germany expected to follow later this year.' Mozilla: 'a new AI model for Smart Window users in the US and Canada, while expanding Smart Window beta access and French-language support to Firefox users in France', plus 'additional European expansion later this year'.
unverified_or_excluded.why_excluded: Both are first-party and they describe France differently - Mistral folds it into the list of markets Mistral powers, Mozilla describes France as receiving beta access and French-language support. Mozilla also declines to name the UK and Germany. Per BRIEF rule 8, the article must print both versions with their publishers and must not pick one or blend them.

unverified_or_excluded.seen_where: Mozilla names 'Mistral Small 4'. Mistral's own post says only 'Mistral models'.

unverified_or_excluded.claim: That Smart Window is new on 2026-09-16.

editorial_brief:
READER AND ANGLE. Written for a Taiwanese general reader who uses Firefox, or who simply wonders why every browser is suddenly shipping an AI assistant. The reader cannot use this yet - the named markets are France, the US and Canada. The article is worth their time for two reasons, and both are transferable. First, it is the clearest example this year of a browser treating the AI model as a slot rather than a fixture: Mozilla says users can still choose from other models, and separately buys web retrieval from a third company. Second, it is a clean teaching case in reading vendor announcements, because two first parties published on the same day and described the same launch differently.

THE CENTRAL FACT TO GET RIGHT. Do not resolve the discrepancy. Mistral's sentence and Mozilla's sentence both go in the article, each with its publisher named. Mistral: France and North America, UK and Germany expected later this year. Mozilla: the model for the US and Canada, France gets beta access and French-language support, and further European expansion is 'planned' with no country named. A reviewer will check whether the article picked a side.

THE SECOND THING TO GET RIGHT. Taiwan and Asia are absent from all three pages. Write that as an absence in what was published, not as an exclusion - Mozilla never enumerates the markets where Smart Window beta exists, so 'not available in Taiwan' would be an inference from silence.

WHAT A READER TAKES AWAY. Three checkable things about any AI feature arriving in software they already use: which model is behind it and whether they can change it; whether the conversation is stored, and where, and what 'by default' means; and whether the feature's availability is about their country or their language - here those two are genuinely different, since France got the language and North America got the model.

SUGGESTED FIVE SECTIONS. (1) What was announced on 2026-09-16 and what Smart Window already was before it (August, beta, months of testing). (2) The two accounts side by side, ending with the required table (max 4 columns: 說法來源 / 市場 / 語言或模型 / 之後的計畫; 3-4 rows; caption dated 2026-09-18) - the table is the natural home for the discrepancy. (3) Model as a slot, not a fixture: still able to choose other models, Exa for retrieval, Mistral Small 4 as one option; diagram goes here. (4) The data sentences and what they do and do not promise - not saved on Mozilla's servers by default, partners agree to zero data retention, context only what the user chooses to share, and the fact that no policy document backs any of it on these pages. (5) What neither company said, and why an announcement that names four countries is still worth reading in a fifth.

ORIGINAL SCENARIO, to be labelled as an editorial example per BRIEF. A reader updates a browser and finds a new assistant panel. The editorial point is the order of the three questions to ask - which model, can I change it, and where does what I type go - and that a good announcement answers all three while a partnership announcement usually answers only the first.

TONE AND SCOPE. Plain, short, no advocacy for any browser and no open-source romance; both companies supply plenty of that themselves and it should be reported as their framing, not adopted. Deliberately out of scope: what open weights mean in depth (covered 2026-02-16); any competition-law angle, since neither company names a regulator; naming any company as the target of Mozilla's 'Big Tech' phrasing; Firefox market share; any hands-on impression.
